title: DWP online services cyber incident, Nov 2026

subject.name: DWP
subject.about: The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) is the UK government department responsible for welfare, pensions and child maintenance policy. It pays the State Pension and working-age, disability and ill-health benefits, such as Universal Credit and PIP, to around 20 million people.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by the Department for Work and Pensions, the UK government, any news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: DWP serves around 20 million claimants and customers across the UK, and some of its online services are offline. It says regular benefit and pension payments are not affected, and it has not said how many people the outage reaches or whether any data was taken.
who_is_affected: People who use DWP's online services, including pensions, Universal Credit, PIP and Tell Us Once. DWP says benefit and pension payments will be paid as normal, though some claimants told the BBC theirs had not arrived. It never messages people asking for bank details.

known.text: DWP says it identified a cyber incident affecting its systems and took some online services offline as a precaution.
Some DWP online services are offline, and no time has been given for their return.
DWP says regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal.
DWP is working with the National Cyber Security Centre to investigate.

not_known.text: What kind of cyber incident it was, and whether anyone got into DWP's systems.
Whether any personal data was accessed or taken. Downing Street says there is currently no evidence of customer data loss.
When the online services will be back.
